newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SET TO GET POST-APARTHEID EDUCATION LAWS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SET TO GET POST-APARTHEID EDUCATION LAWS.

text.p: South Africa is set to finally enshrine post-apartheid education in law after a parliamentary committee approved a new bill despite protests from opposition parties.
The bill proposed by Nelson Mandela's majority African National Congress would scrap decades-old apartheid education and make schooling compulsory for children of all races.
Under South Africa's old segregationist laws, children of different races had separate state education, with whites getting by far the largest share of the funding.

The opposition National Party, which invented apartheid and then scrapped it with an apology over 40 years later, voted against the bill, saying it would take away too much of the power of school boards.
Other opposition parties abstained from the committee vote.
The ANC has argued that boards at formerly whites-only schools have tried to keep black pupils out of their classrooms.
There were racial clashes in several areas around the country when provincial governments ordered old whites-only schools -- which parents wanted to keep that way -- to admit black children.
The bill will now go to parliament's national assembly and senate for debate and voting.
